{"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

{"reference_id": "", "content": ""Love the Way You Lie" is a song by American rapper Eminem featuring Barbadian singer Rihanna from Eminem's seventh studio album Recovery (2010). Skylar Grey wrote and recorded a demo of the song alongside producer Alex da Kid. Eminem wrote the verses and chose Rihanna to sing the chorus, resulting in a collaboration influenced by their past experiences in difficult relationships. Recording sessions were held in Ferndale, Michigan, and Dublin, Ireland. Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

Interscope Records released the song in June 2010 as the second single from Recovery. Critics praised its melody but were divided on its thematic aspects such as poignancy and accuracy. Eminem promoted the single with performances at the 2010 Electronic Entertainment Expo, the MTV Video Music Awards and festivals. The music video, directed by Joseph Kahn, stars Dominic Monaghan and Megan Fox as lovers in a violent relationship and shows Eminem and Rihanna in front of a burning house. The video met with a mixed reception due to scenes of domestic violence. Reporters suggested that the song and its accompanying video were influenced by Eminem's and Rihanna's abusive relationships with their respective ex-lovers, Kim Scott and Chris Brown.

Critics listed "Love the Way You Lie" among the best tracks of 2010 and of Eminem's career. The song won many awards and received five Grammy nominations. It is Eminem's best-selling single and ranked number one on several record charts, including the US Billboard Hot 100 for seven weeks. The single sold over 12 million copies in the US and 1.5 million in the UK. Musical acts such as Cher Lloyd and the Band Perry have performed cover versions. Rihanna has said that the theme of domestic violence, a topic on which she claims many people do not have insight, is what makes the song impactful. She later recorded with him again on "Love the Way You Lie (Part II)", narrated mostly from her perspective. "Love the Way You Lie" peaked at number one in 22 countries.

Writing and production
Rihanna with red, long hair and a dress with floral patterns. Her left hand is raised and her right-hand holds a microphone near her mouth.
Rihanna's approval of the song's topic ultimately influenced her decision to work with Eminem.
The development of "Love the Way You Lie" began with the backing track and hook melody, which was created by British hip hop producer Alex da Kid.[2] When making a track, he explained that he spends hours making loops and produces an electronic drum rhythm before adding live instrumentation. The drums are sampled from live recordings he saved.[3] Alex da Kid recorded an acoustic guitar for the verses with a Neumann U 87 microphone and an Avid Mbox audio interface. He told Sound on Sound magazine that this song had given him an opportunity to reintroduce live guitar in hip hop music.[3] During the session, he used Waves RVerb and REQ equalization on his main kick track and a MaxxBass plug-in on two others.[2]

Writing began in late 2009, when singer Skylar Grey resided at the Artula Retreat in Bandon, Oregon,[4] and wrote songs.[5] Later, in New York City, she visited her Universal Music publisher, Jennifer Blakeman, to seek help presenting her work;[5][6] Blakeman suggested she collaborate with Alex da Kid.[5] The producer emailed Grey his track, which suggested a theme of abusive romantic relationships to her as she spontaneously sang lyrics to the melody.[7] She told the Los Angeles Times that she was in an abusive relationship with the music industry: "I love it so much, and I give it all that I have, yet it beats me down."[8] This idea inspired her writing,[8] a process she found came naturally, as if she were creating an alternative pop song for herself.[9] She wrote the chorus to "Love the Way You Lie" in fifteen minutes and recorded vocals for Alex da Kid's demo.[5][10]

In early 2010, Alex da Kid offered Shady Records senior director Rigo Morales some backing tracks.[11] Morales enjoyed the tracks and sent them to Eminem, who was seeking a different musical approach for his next album.[11] Impressed with Alex da Kid's work, Eminem asked for more tracks and subsequently heard "Love the Way You Lie". He chose it and told his manager Paul Rosenberg he wanted to collaborate with the Barbadian singer Rihanna.[11] Eminem told Skyrock, "It's one of those tracks that I felt like only she could pull it off."[12] Rosenberg sent the track to Rihanna, who accepted Eminem's request "at the last moment."[11] Eminem wrote the rapped verses to the song.[10]

Rihanna has also said she joined the collaboration because she could relate to the theme of the song, as she and Eminem had been in difficult relationships on "different ends of the table".[13] Eminem had released the songs "'97 Bonnie & Clyde" (1998) and "Kim" (2000), in which he fantasizes, respectively, about murdering and verbally abusing his then-wife Kim Scott.[14] They had divorced in 2001 and again in 2006 after a remarriage.[15] In February 2009, Rihanna's relationship with the R&B singer Chris Brown had ended following his felony assault on her.[16] Rihanna described "Love the Way You Lie" as unique, realistic and deep, saying that it "broke down the cycle of domestic violence" because few people had insight on the topic.[13][17][18]

Recording
Mike Strange recorded and mixed Eminem's vocals at Effigy Studios in Ferndale, Michigan.[19] The sessions took two days.[20] Strange edited the vocals with D-Verb—a reverberation software—and an Extra Long Delay plug-in. He preferred to make few changes; for "Love the Way You Lie" he almost exclusively used board compression and console equalization. Strange used the Bricasti and Eventide Reverb 2016 mixing tools for "brighter" reverberation. Detroit musician Luis Resto has contributed to the arrangement on many of Eminem's songs, but did not do so for "Love the Way You Lie". According to Strange, "Everything we needed was already in the track, apart from the vocals."[2] Two to three weeks after the sessions, Alex da Kid arrived to help mix and master the track.[11] He wanted to replace the acoustic guitar on the demo, but Eminem chose to keep it.[3] Strange said, "It was simply a matter of trying to match and then to improve on the demo [Alex da Kid]'d sent us."[2] Strange's brother Joe engineered the track.[19]

Rihanna's recording sessions took place at Sun Studios in Dublin, Ireland, and were engineered by Marcos Tovar. The R&B songwriter Makeba Riddick provided additional vocal production.[19] Strange used equalization, compression and reverberation but left the vocal balance. He assumed that Rihanna was satisfied with her recorded vocals and did not make major changes on her seven stereo vocal tracks.[2]

question: What is the taboo name of Lac Long Quan, and who are his father and mother?
answer:
In Vietnamese mythology, **Lac Long Quan** (also known as **Lạc Long Quân**) is a legendary figure associated with the creation of the Vietnamese people. According to traditional lore:

- **Taboo Name**: The name **Lac Long Quan** itself is considered his taboo name. In some interpretations, this reflects the reverence for his divine status, as using his full name might be seen as disrespectful. However, this is more of a cultural nuance than a strict taboo, as his name is widely recognized in Vietnamese history and folklore.

- **Parents**:  
  - **Father**: **Lord of the Dragon** (a divine being associated with water and power).  
  - **Mother**: **Lady of the Snake** (a celestial figure linked to earth and fertility).  

Lac Long Quan is celebrated as a cultural hero, and his story is central to the legend of the **Lạc Long Quân - Âu Cơ** myth, which explains the origins of the Vietnamese people. His name and lineage are deeply symbolic in Vietnamese cultural identity.

answer:

This union is central to the mythological narrative of the Bach Viet's origins, with Lac Long Quan's lineage playing a pivotal role in the formation of the nation.

- **Spouse:** Daughter of De Lai (named Au Co).
- **Children:** 100 sons, who are the progenitors of the Bach Viet people.

question: When they separated, how did Lac Long Quan and Au Co divide their children?
answer:
In the legend of **Lac Long Quan** (a dragon lord) and **Au Co** (a buffalo princess), their separation and division of children are central to the myth. According to the most widely accepted version:

1. **Division by Gender**:  
   After their separation, Lac Long Quan and Au Co divided their children based on **gender**. Lac Long Quan took the **sons**, while Au Co retained the **daughters**. This division symbolized the merging of their respective lineages—Lac Long Quan's dragon heritage and Au Co's buffalo ancestry.

2. **Number of Children**:  
   The story mentions they had **five children** in total. However, the exact number and names of the children vary across different versions of the legend. Some accounts specify that Au Co's daughter, **Mỵ Nương** (later known as **Lạc Hồn**), became the queen of the Cham people, while Lac Long Quan's sons were associated with the northern Vietnamese dynasties.

3. **Symbolism**:  
   The division of children reflects the **union of two distinct cultural and mythical lineages** (dragon and buffalo) to form the foundation of the Vietnamese people. It also underscores the themes of **duality, separation, and reconciliation** in the legend.

**Note**: Variations in the story exist across regional and historical sources, but the core narrative of dividing children by gender remains consistent.

Growing up, he, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were sent to study both literature and martial arts with teacher Truong Van Hien. Truong Van Hien was a retainer of Truong Van Hanh, and Truong Van Hanh was the teacher of Nguyen Phuc Luan – Nguyen Anh's father. After Truong Van Hanh was harmed by the powerful courtier Truong Phuc Loan, Truong Van Hien fled to Binh Dinh. It was this teacher who discovered Nguyen Hue's abilities and advised the three brothers to rebel to build a great enterprise. Legend has it that the prophecy "Tay khoi nghia, Bac thu cong" (Rebel in the West, achieve success in the North) originated from Truong Van Hien.[14] Legend also has it that Nguyen Hue, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were all highly skilled in martial arts and were the founders of several Binh Dinh martial arts styles. question: What were the officials in charge of affairs under Hung Vuong called and what were their hereditary characteristics?
answer: Under Hung Vuong's rule, officials in charge of affairs were called **Bo Chinh**. Their hereditary characteristic was referred to as **phu dao**, meaning they passed down their positions from father to son through hereditary succession. This system ensured continuity in governance by allowing the sons of these officials to inherit their roles.

question: During which Zhou king's reign did our country first visit the Zhou dynasty, and what was offered?
answer:
The question appears to conflate historical timelines and contexts. The Zhou dynasty (1046–256 BCE) was a Chinese dynasty, and there is no recorded historical event of "our country" (assuming China) visiting the Zhou dynasty as a foreign entity, since the Zhou dynasty itself was the central power in ancient China. 

If the question refers to interactions between the Zhou dynasty and other regions or states, here are key points:

1. **Early Zhou Dynasty (Western Zhou, 1046–771 BCE):**  
   - The Zhou dynasty was established after overthrowing the Shang dynasty. Its early interactions were primarily with vassal states within China, such as the state of Qi, which was a key ally. These were not "visits" but rather political and military alliances.

2. **Later Zhou Dynasty (Eastern Zhou, 771–256 BCE):**  
   - During the Spring and Autumn (771–476 BCE) and Warring States (475–221 BCE) periods, the Zhou royal court lost its political power, and the Zhou king became a symbolic figure. States like Qin, Chu, and Qi vied for dominance, but these were internal conflicts, not foreign visits.

3. **Possible Confusion with Other Dynasties:**  
   - If the question refers to interactions between the Zhou dynasty and the Xia or Shang dynasties (earlier dynasties), these were not "visits" but rather periods of conflict or succession. For example, the Zhou dynasty was founded by King Wu of Zhou after defeating the Shang.

**Conclusion:**  
There is no historical record of a specific "first visit" from another country to the Zhou dynasty. The Zhou dynasty's interactions were primarily with vassal states within China, and its own establishment marked the end of the Shang dynasty. If the question refers to a different context (e.g., cultural exchanges or diplomatic missions), additional clarification would be needed.

Nguyen Hue was born in the year of Quy Dau 1753, the 13th year of the Canh Hung reign under King Le Hien Tong of the Later Le Dynasty. He was also known as Quang Binh,[11] Van Hue[12], or Ho Thom. Later, local people often called him Duc Ong Binh (Lord Binh)[13] or Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight).[8] According to Quang Trung anh hùng dân tộc (Quang Trung the National Hero), "Nguyen Hue had curly hair, textured skin, eyes that flashed like lightning, a voice as resonant as a bell, agile, strong, and brave." The book Tây Sơn lược also described Quang Trung's eyes: "at night, when sitting without a lamp, the light from his eyes illuminated the whole mat."

Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent: The books Đại Nam thực lục chính biên, Đại Nam chính biên liệt truyện, and Tây Sơn thủy mạt khảo all agree on the order of the three Tay Son brothers, affirming that: "The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue"; The people of old Quy Nhon prefecture passed down that: Nguyen Nhac traded betel in his youth, so he was called Anh Hai Trau (Brother Two Betel), Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom), and Nguyen Lu was called Thay Tu Lu (Master Four Lu).[a] According to letters from Western missionaries active in Dai Viet at that time, such as Labartette, Eyet, and Varen, Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother. After Truong Van Hanh was harmed by the powerful courtier Truong Phuc Loan, Truong Van Hien fled to Binh Dinh. {"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

Origins and Education

Origins of the Tay Son lineage

According to the books Khâm định Việt sử Thông giám cương mục and Đại Nam thực lục: Nguyen Hue's ancestors were from Hung Nguyen district, Nghe An region. question: Why did Thuc Vuong harbor resentment towards Hung Vuong?
answer:
Thuc Vuong (Thuc Phu) harbored resentment towards Hung Vuong (the Hung Kings) due to a historical rivalry between the two dynasties during the early formation of the Vietnamese state. This conflict is central to the legend of the "Battle of the Two Kings" (Hung vs. Thuc), which symbolizes the struggle for power and legitimacy in ancient Vietnam. Key reasons for the resentment include:

1. **Political Ambitions**: Thuc Phu, a general under the Hung Kings, later rebelled to establish the Thuc Dynasty. His resentment likely stemmed from a desire to seize power and challenge the existing ruling dynasty, viewing the Hung Kings as obstacles to his ambitions.

2. **Succession Disputes**: The Thuc Dynasty's rise to power may have been fueled by disputes over succession or the legitimacy of the Hung Kings' rule. Thuc Phu might have felt marginalized or wronged by the Hung Kings' leadership, prompting his rebellion.

3. **Power Struggles**: The conflict between the dynasties reflects broader tensions over territorial control and governance. Thuc Vuong's resentment would have been driven by a desire to assert dominance over the region, leading to prolonged warfare and rivalry.

4. **Legitimacy and Legacy**: The Thuc Dynasty's attempt to overthrow the Hung Kings was not just a political move but also a contest over historical narrative. Thuc Vuong's resentment may have been tied to reclaiming or redefining the legacy of leadership in the region.

This rivalry is a foundational element of Vietnamese history, symbolizing the early struggles to unify the country under a single ruling authority. The conflict ultimately contributed to the eventual unification of the north and south under the Later Le Dynasty, with the Hung Kings' legacy preserved as the spiritual foundation of the nation.

question: Who were the two figures that came to propose to Mi Nuong at the same time, and what condition did Hung Vuong set?
answer:
The two figures who came to propose to Mi Nuong at the same time were **Son Tinh (Mountain Spirit)** and **Thuy Tinh (Water Spirit)**.  

**Hung Vuong's condition** was that whoever brought **sufficient betrothal gifts first** would be granted the hand of Mi Nuong in marriage. Son Tinh arrived first with lavish gifts (jewels, gold, silver, etc.), securing the marriage, while Thuy Tinh arrived later and resented this, leading to the legendary feud between the two spirits.

After Truong Van Hanh was harmed by the powerful courtier Truong Phuc Loan, Truong Van Hien fled to Binh Dinh. It was this teacher who discovered Nguyen Hue's abilities and advised the three brothers to rebel to build a great enterprise. Legend has it that the prophecy "Tay khoi nghia, Bac thu cong" (Rebel in the West, achieve success in the North) originated from Truong Van Hien.[14] Legend also has it that Nguyen Hue, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were all highly skilled in martial arts and were the founders of several Binh Dinh martial arts styles. Recording sessions were held in Ferndale, Michigan, and Dublin, Ireland. Backed by guitar, piano and violin, the track is a midtempo hip-hop ballad with a pop refrain, sung by Rihanna, and describes two lovers who refuse to separate despite being in an abusive relationship.

{"reference_id": "", "content": "Quang Trung (Chinese characters: 光中, 1753 – September 16, 1792), whose pre-coronation title was Bac Binh Vuong (北平王 - Prince of Northern Peace), birth name Ho Thom (胡𦹳), originally from Nghe An and later renamed Nguyen Hue (阮惠), was a Vietnamese politician and military leader. He was the 2nd emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty after his older brother, Emperor Thai Duc Nguyen Nhac, abdicated and passed the throne to him.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

Origins and Education

question: Who later inherited Thuc Vuong's resentment and conquered Van Lang?
answer:
The answer is **Thuc Phan**. 

According to the reference text, after Thuc Vuong's initial resentment toward the king's decision to marry his daughter Mi Nuong to Son Tinh, he instructed his descendants to destroy Van Lang and conquer the country. His descendant, **Thuc Phan** (a figure from Vietnamese mythology), possessed courage and strategic prowess. He eventually launched an attack and conquered Van Lang, fulfilling Thuc Vuong's vengeance. This is detailed in the legend recounting the conflict between Thuc Vuong (a mythical northern ruler) and the Van Lang kingdom during the Hung Vuong era.

Nguyen Hue and his two brothers, known as the Tay Son heroes (Tây Sơn tam kiệt), were the leaders of the Tay Son uprising that ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war between the two feudal groups of Trinh in the north and Nguyen in the south, overthrowing these two groups along with the Later Le Dynasty, ending the division of Dang Trong (Inner Realm) and Dang Ngoai (Outer Realm) that lasted for 2 centuries. In addition, Quang Trung was also the one who defeated the invasions of Dai Viet by Siam from the south and the Great Qing from the north. He personally commanded troops from the age of 18, and over 20 consecutive years, he fought in dozens of major battles without losing a single one.

Historian Phan Huy Le evaluated that "Quang Trung was not only a brilliant military leader but also a politician with exceptional talent"[1]. With a progressive vision, in just 3 years, he successively proposed many progressive reform plans in economics, culture, education, military,... to build the country and absorb modern science and technology from the West.[2] Regarding personnel, he issued an edict seeking talented people and heavily utilized many talents such as Ngo Thi Nham, Phan Huy Ich, Nguyen Thiep, Nguyen Huy Luong,... In terms of the military, he built an army equipped with modern weapons. Economically, he reformed the taxation and land systems, encouraged handicrafts, and expanded foreign trade with the West. Regarding education, he improved the examination system in a practical direction, promulgated policies to encourage learning, encouraged the use of pure Vietnamese Nom script instead of Han script, reorganized redundant temples, and eradicated superstitions. Historians highly appreciate these reforms because they had a very progressive tendency, surpassing contemporary Asian countries, and could bring the country out of the stagnation that had lasted over 100 years under the Trinh–Nguyen feudal system. Even much later (1822), overseas Chinese who lived in Hue under the Tay Son era still reminisced about Nguyen Hue's rule; they commented to a British merchant that Quang Trung ruled more mildly and fairly than the Nguyen dynasty kings (Gia Long and Minh Mang)[3] (see details at progressive reforms of King Quang Trung).

The active life of Nguyen Hue made a decisive contribution to the cause of national reunification of the Tay Son dynasty[4]. After 20 years of continuous warfare and 3 years of ruling the country, when the country's situation began to show positive changes, Quang Trung died suddenly at the age of 39. After his death, the Tay Son Dynasty weakened rapidly. His successor, Quang Toan, was still too young (9 years old) to lead Dai Viet; the royal court fell into internal conflict and failed to continue resisting Nguyen Anh.

Nguyen Hue is listed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism as one of the 14 typical national heroes of Vietnam.[5] Many schools and streets in localities are named Quang Trung and Nguyen Hue.

question: How many years did the Hong Bang dynasty last in total, and in which years did it begin and end?
answer:
The Hong Bang dynasty (Hung Kings' reign) is traditionally associated with the legendary era of the Hung Kings in Vietnamese history. According to the provided documents and historical accounts:

- **Duration**: The dynasty is said to have lasted **18 generations** of kings, with each king ruling for **10 years**, totaling **180 years**. This is a traditional count rather than a precise historical timeline.  
- **Start and End Years**: The documents do not specify exact start and end years. However, traditional Vietnamese chronicles often cite the Hong Bang dynasty as beginning around **2876 BCE** (the legendary founding of the Van Lang kingdom by Hung Vuong) and ending in **258 BCE** (the transition to the Later Le Dynasty). This would make the dynasty last **2,618 years**, but this is a mythological timeline rather than a historically verified period.  

**Note**: The provided texts focus on legends and early historical events rather than precise dates, so the answer relies on traditional accounts rather than documented historical records.

question: Who were the three brothers of the Tay Son movement?
answer:
The three brothers of the Tay Son movement were **Nguyen Nhac** (阮 Nhac), **Nguyen Hue** (阮 Hue), and **Nguyen Lu** (阮 Lu). They were collectively known as the **Tay Son heroes** (*Tây Sơn tam kiệt*) and played pivotal roles in the Tay Son uprising (1771–1802), which ended the Trinh–Nguyen civil war in Vietnam. 

1. **Nguyen Nhac** (eldest):  
   - Served as the first emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty.  
   - Abdicated the throne in 1788 to allow his younger brother, Nguyen Hue, to succeed him.  

2. **Nguyen Hue** (middle):  
   - Became the **second emperor** of the Tay Son Dynasty.  
   - Renowned as a brilliant military leader and reformer, he unified Vietnam, defeated foreign invasions (e.g., Siam and Qing), and implemented progressive policies.  
   - Died suddenly in 1792 at age 39, leading to the decline of the Tay Son Dynasty.  

3. **Nguyen Lu** (youngest):  
   - The third brother, who later became the third emperor of the Tay Son Dynasty.  
   - His reign was short-lived and marked by internal strife, as the dynasty weakened after Nguyen Hue's death.  

Together, the three brothers led the Tay Son movement to end the feudal division of Vietnam and establish a brief period of centralized rule. Their legacy is celebrated in Vietnamese history for its military achievements and reforms.

question: At what age did Quang Trung die, and what happened to the Tay Son Dynasty after his death?
answer:
Quang Trung (Nguyen Hue) died at the age of **39** in **1792**. His death marked the beginning of the decline of the Tay Son Dynasty. After his passing, the dynasty faced significant internal strife and external pressures:

1. **Succession Struggles**:  
   Quang Trung's brothers, **Nguyen Nhac** (the eldest) and **Nguyen Lu** (the third), inherited power but lacked his military and political acumen. Nguyen Nhac focused on consolidating control in the north, while Nguyen Lu prioritized the south. This division weakened the dynasty's unity and ability to respond to threats.

2. **Rise of the Nguyen Dynasty**:  
   The Nguyen family, led by **Nguyen Anh** (later Emperor Gia Long), exploited the Tay Son's internal divisions. Nguyen Anh allied with the Trinh lords in the north and launched a campaign to overthrow the Tay Son. By **1802**, the Nguyen forces defeated the Tay Son, ending their rule and establishing the Nguyen dynasty as the dominant power in Vietnam.

3. **Collapse of the Tay Son**:  
   The dynasty's fragmentation, combined with the Nguyen's military superiority, led to its collapse. The Tay Son's legacy, however, remains significant as they briefly unified Vietnam and challenged the traditional Le and Trinh feudal systems.

Upon ascending the throne, Hung Vuong set the national name as Van Lang (this country bordered the South Sea to the east, Ba Thuc to the west, Dong Dinh lake to the north, and Ho Ton - which is Champa, now Quang Nam - to the south). He divided the country into 15 administrative regions: Giao Chi, Chu Dien, Vu Ninh, Phuc Loc, Viet Thuong, Ninh Hai, Duong Tuyen, Luc Hai, Vu Dinh, Hoai Hoan, Cuu Chan, Binh Van, Tan Hung, Cuu Duc; all were vassal lands of Hung Vuong; while the region called Van Lang was where the king established the capital. He appointed civil generals called Lac Hau, and military generals called Lac Tuong. The king's sons were called Quan Lang, and daughters were called Mi Nuong. Officials in charge of affairs were called Bo Chinh; their hereditary succession from father to son was called phu dao. Kings of all generations were called Hung Vuong. At that time, the people living in the forests and mountains saw that the rivers and streams had shrimp and fish, so they invited each other to catch fish for food, but were often harmed by water monsters (thuong luong). [3b] They came to report this to the king. The king said: "The barbarians in the mountains are different from aquatic species; those aquatic species favor their own kind and hate other species, which is why you are harmed by them." The king then told everyone to use ink to tattoo images of water monsters on their bodies. From then on, the water monsters saw them and no longer bit or harmed them. The tattooing custom of the Bach Viet people probably started from there.

Nguyen Hue was born in the year of Quy Dau 1753, the 13th year of the Canh Hung reign under King Le Hien Tong of the Later Le Dynasty. He was also known as Quang Binh,[11] Van Hue[12], or Ho Thom. Later, local people often called him Duc Ong Binh (Lord Binh)[13] or Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight).[8] According to Quang Trung anh hùng dân tộc (Quang Trung the National Hero), "Nguyen Hue had curly hair, textured skin, eyes that flashed like lightning, a voice as resonant as a bell, agile, strong, and brave." The book Tây Sơn lược also described Quang Trung's eyes: "at night, when sitting without a lamp, the light from his eyes illuminated the whole mat."

Regarding the birth order of Nguyen Hue and Nguyen Lu among the brothers, documentary sources are inconsistent: The books Đại Nam thực lục chính biên, Đại Nam chính biên liệt truyện, and Tây Sơn thủy mạt khảo all agree on the order of the three Tay Son brothers, affirming that: "The eldest is Nhac, next is Lu, and then Hue"; The people of old Quy Nhon prefecture passed down that: Nguyen Nhac traded betel in his youth, so he was called Anh Hai Trau (Brother Two Betel), Nguyen Hue was also named Thom, so he was called Chu Ba Thom (Uncle Three Thom), and Nguyen Lu was called Thay Tu Lu (Master Four Lu).[a] According to letters from Western missionaries active in Dai Viet at that time, such as Labartette, Eyet, and Varen, Nguyen Hue was Nguyen Lu's younger brother. Nguyen Lu was called Duc Ong Bay (Lord Seven) and Nguyen Hue was Duc Ong Tam (Lord Eight); Le Trong Ham in the book Minh đô sử argued that Ho Phi Phuc fathered "Nhac, Lu, then two daughters, and then Hue".

Growing up, he, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were sent to study both literature and martial arts with teacher Truong Van Hien. Truong Van Hien was a retainer of Truong Van Hanh, and Truong Van Hanh was the teacher of Nguyen Phuc Luan – Nguyen Anh's father. After Truong Van Hanh was harmed by the powerful courtier Truong Phuc Loan, Truong Van Hien fled to Binh Dinh. It was this teacher who discovered Nguyen Hue's abilities and advised the three brothers to rebel to build a great enterprise. Legend has it that the prophecy "Tay khoi nghia, Bac thu cong" (Rebel in the West, achieve success in the North) originated from Truong Van Hien.[14] Legend also has it that Nguyen Hue, Nguyen Nhac, and Nguyen Lu were all highly skilled in martial arts and were the founders of several Binh Dinh martial arts styles. During the reign of the 6th Hung King, in Phu Dong village, Vu Ninh region, there was a wealthy family who had a son. By the time he was over three years old, he ate well and grew big but did not know how to speak or laugh. At a time when there was urgent news of danger in the country, the king sent envoys to find someone who could repel the enemy. On that day, the child suddenly spoke, telling his mother to invite the royal envoy in, and said: "Please grant me a sword and a horse, the king needs not worry about anything." The king granted him a sword and a horse; the child immediately rode the horse, brandished the sword, and charged forward with the royal army following behind, defeating the enemy troops at the foot of Vu Ninh mountain. The enemy troops turned their spears against each other, with many casualties; the survivors all bowed down, revered the child as a heavenly general, and immediately surrendered. The child rode his horse [4a] into the sky and departed. The king ordered the child's home garden to be renovated into a temple for annual sacrifices. Later, Ly Thai To granted him the title Xung Thien Than Vuong. (The temple is located next to Kien So pagoda, Phu Dong village).

During the reign of King Cheng of Zhou [1063-1026 BC], our country of Viet visited the Zhou dynasty for the first time (it is unclear during which Hung King's reign), claiming to be the Viet Thuong clan, and offered a white pheasant. The Duke of Zhou said: "If our political decrees do not reach them, a gentleman does not treat them as his subjects," and then ordered the construction of a south-pointing chariot to escort the envoys back to their country.

At the end of the Hung Vuong era, the king had a daughter named Mi Nuong, who was remarkably beautiful. Thuc Vuong heard of her and came to propose marriage. The king wanted to agree, but the Hung Hau advised against it: "They want to conquer our country and are only using marriage as an excuse." Because of this, Thuc Vuong harbored resentment. The king, wanting to find a worthy person to marry her to, told his subjects: "This daughter is of fairy descent; only someone with sufficient talent and virtue can be my son-in-law." At that time, two men arrived from outside and bowed in the courtyard to propose. The king found it strange; when asked, they replied that one was [4b] Son Tinh (Mountain Spirit) and the other was Thuy Tinh (Water Spirit), both from the great realm, who had heard the king had a divine daughter and made bold to come request her hand. The king said: "I have only one daughter, how can I have both of you as worthy sons-in-law?" He then set a condition that the next day, whoever brought sufficient betrothal gifts first would marry her. The two men obeyed, bowed in gratitude, and left. The next day, Son Tinh brought jewels, gold, silver, mountain birds, and forest beasts as gifts. The king kept his promise and married his daughter to him. Son Tinh took his wife to live on a high peak of Tan Vien mountain. Thuy Tinh also arrived with betrothal gifts later; furious and regretful that he was too late, he summoned clouds and rain, raised the waters to flood the land, and led aquatic creatures in pursuit. The king and Son Tinh stretched iron nets across the upper reaches of the Tu Liem river to block them. Thuy Tinh took another river, from Ly Nhan to the foot of Quang Oai mountain, then followed the banks up to the Hat river estuary, out to the great river, and turned into the Da river to attack Tan Vien. Everywhere he went, he dug deep abysses and swamps, storing water to plot a surprise attack. Son Tinh possessed divine powers of transformation; he called [5a] the barbarians to weave bamboo into water barriers, and used crossbows to shoot downwards. The scaled and shelled creatures hit by arrows all fled. Ultimately, Thuy Tinh could not invade Tan Vien mountain. (Legend has it that from then on, Son Tinh and Thuy Tinh harbored a generational feud, and every year during the high water season, they often fought each other).

Tan Vien mountain is a high mountain range in our Viet country, and its sacredness is highly responsive. After Mi Nuong married Son Tinh, Thuc Vuong was furious and instructed his descendants to destroy Van Lang and seize the country. In the time of his descendant, Thuc Phan, who possessed courage and strategy, he attacked and conquered the country.
